title: Offline deployment feasibility discussion — Citrine Pathology
summary: Initial feasibility call to understand Citrine's constraints for an air-gapped, on-prem inference deployment. Covered hardware inventory, offline update mechanisms, compliance (SOC2/ISO), network restrictions, and POC success criteria. Redwood AE/SE outlined high-level architecture options (single-node vs small cluster), secure update workflow, and data-at-rest/in-transit protections. Agreed next steps: send security pack, hardware sizing proposal, and schedule a deeper technical workshop on image signing & update automation.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Gupta (Citrine CTO), Evan Torres (Infra), Lena Ortiz (Compliance)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Alex from Redwood Inference here, AE covering Citrine pathol— patholoogy? sorry, Citrine Pathology. Priya's with me, she's our SE and will go deep on the on-prem architecture later.
[00:10] Dr. Maya Gupta: Great thanks, Alex. We're mainly trying to understand if we can run Redwood in our locked network. No outgoing internet allowed from the inference nodes, strict change control, and monthly audited updates.
[00:20] Evan Torres: And to add, we only have two racks allocated for this project. Each rack can host up to four 3U servers, and our current GPUs are mixed A100 40GB and two H100 80GB nodes that are on dedicated VLANs.
[00:33] Priya Desai: Okay cool, that helps. Priya, Redwood SE. Quick note: we support a few private deployment topologies — single-node for low concurrency, small cluster for higher throughput, or a dedicated pool with an airgapped control plane depending on your change control needs.
[00:45] Lena Ortiz: Compliance question up front — we need to know about key management. Can Redwood integrate with an on-prem HSM for KMS? We cannot have keys stored in a third party.
[00:55] Priya Desai: Yes, integrating with customer-managed KMS/HSM is a typical requirement. For private deployments we can use your HSM for signing and key material; in an airgap setup the control plane is still optional to be offline. We'll need a secure mechanism to boot strap credentials, typically via an operator-run key ceremony or manual injection.
[01:12] Dr. Maya Gupta: How do you handle updates to the runtime and models? Our security team insists on image signing, whitelisting, and a formal approval before any change gets installed.
[01:23] Priya Desai: We have an image signing workflow — images and artifacts are signed with a private key. In redwood privet — sorry, Redwood Private — the node will verify signatures before accepting new images. For air-gapped customers, we provide a signed artifact bundle and a checklist for offline transfer. Customers import via USB or an approved secure transfer appliance and the node verifies the signature and checksum.
[01:42] Evan Torres: USB is allowed but only via our transfer workstation that has strict scanning. We can't have the nodes reach out to any external registry.
[01:49] Alex Kim: That fits the pattern we've seen. We'll document an offline update runbook — will include signed tar bundles, SHA256 checks, and an operator approval step in the console.
[02:00] Lena Ortiz: Audit logs — retention and tamper-evidence are important. We need immutable logs for any model change and operator action.
[02:09] Priya Desai: We can write logs locally and ship them out via a secure pull from your log aggregator. For tamper-evidence we recommend using signed append-only logs; we can integrate with your SIEM and provide log export hooks. Also you can route audit events to your HSM-backed signing service.
[02:26] Dr. Maya Gupta: On performance: our inference needs are mostly batch pathology slide processing, occasionally live consult sessions. Latency isn't as strict as consumer LLMs but throughput and reliable tokenization are important. We want to avoid large token blowups.
[02:40] Priya Desai: Understood. For batch workloads we recommend a small cluster (2-4 nodes) to allow parallel processing; for intermittent live sessions a single-node with prewarmed KV cache may be acceptable. We also suggested quantized models to fit into 40GB GPUs — that would let you utilize A100 40GB capacity without needing H100s for everything.
[02:58] Evan Torres: Do you support half precision quant or 4-bit quant options? Our infra team prefers lower-precision if accuracy isn't impacted.
[03:07] Priya Desai: We support quantized variants and can do per-model recommendations based on your eval set. We'll include model quality vs cost tradeoffs in the sizing doc.
[03:18] Alex Kim: A few quick qualification items — timeline? budget? stakeholders?
[03:24] Dr. Maya Gupta: Timeline: we need a POC in the next 6 weeks to show to the board. Budget: capped for the POC but we can expand for production. Stakeholders: me, Evan, and Lena. Also the pathology lab director will review accuracy.
[03:38] Priya Desai: Good, 6 weeks is feasible for a scoped POC. Our typical POC for air-gapped goes: site readiness -> transfer test -> runtime + sample model deploy -> throughput validation -> security sign-off.
[03:52] Evan Torres: A question on network: can Redwood run its control plane outside the airgapped network and just send signed image bundles? Or do we need the whole control plane on-prem?
[04:03] Priya Desai: Options: 1) Fully offline private: control plane also runs inside your VPC or on-prem cluster — no external comms. 2) Hybrid: a control plane outside that orchestrates but never touches PHI, and nodes pull signed artifacts. In your case with no outbound from nodes, we'd do full on-prem control plane or a strictly one-way transfer process.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: On SSO — our engineers want SAML/SSO integration for the admin console but we don't want any auth traffic going over the internet. Can you support SSO via our internal IdP?
[04:36] Alex Kim: Yes, SAML works with on-prem IdPs. For airgapped installs we integrate with your internal IdP endpoint; if that's not reachable we can rely on short-lived local admin tokens with rotation.
[04:48] Dr. Maya Gupta: Are there any audit artifacts or compliance docs we can get? SOC2 scope, encryption algorithms, and third party subprocessor list?
[04:57] Alex Kim: We'll send our SOC2 summary, threat model, and a security pack. It includes KMS options, supported algorithms (AES-256, TLS1.3), and a list of third party libs. For on-prem we minimize external processors; you get full control.
[05:12] Evan Torres: About hardware: our power budget per rack is 12kW nominal, 3-phase. Cooling is standard; we can't support liquid cooled chassis. Any recommended server models?
[05:23] Priya Desai: We'll include a hardware compatibility matrix. For A100 40GB it’s standard 3U 4GPU boxes; for H100 we generally need 4U or specialized chassis and you mentioned you have two of those already. We'll call out power draw and peak. Also note that if you want to use quantized models, you can reduce memory pressure.
[05:44] Dr. Maya Gupta: Can we keep PHI on the nodes? We need to ensure data at rest is encrypted, and backups are under our control.
[05:53] Priya Desai: Yes, data-at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys is supported. Backups remain in your environment — we recommend encrypted snapshots that you manage.
[06:03] Alex Kim: Quick note — in some airgapped installs we've used an approved jump server for artifact transfer and integrity validation. Does that align with your policies?
[06:12] Evan Torres: Yes, we've got a transfer workstation that scans and logs every artifact. We can integrate the signing verification step there as part of the SOP.
[06:18] Priya Desai: Great. Let's run a short walkthrough of an example offline update flow: 1) Redwood builds signed image bundle, 2) Alex sends bundle to Citrine, 3) Citrine transfer workstation verifies signature and checksum, 4) Operator uploads to node, 5) Node verifies signature via local key/cert and applies update. Any auto rollback?
[06:38] Dr. Maya Gupta: We want an automatic safe rollback if the new image fails health checks. Can Redwood support that?
[06:43] Priya Desai: Yes, we can do a staged deploy with a canary on a single node, health checks, and auto rollback. In airgapped mode the operator can still approve canary or we can default to automatic rollback on failure.
[06:58] Evan Torres: How are secrets handled on nodes? We want minimal persistent secrets.
[07:03] Priya Desai: Secrets are injected at boot and can be rotated using your HSM: short-lived tokens, or a sealed envelope pattern where key material is decrypted only at runtime. We'll recommend best practices in the runbook.
[07:16] Alex Kim: Any blockers you foresee that would prevent a POC?
[07:20] Dr. Maya Gupta: Two potential blockers: 1) Our security team wants signed SBOMs for any container images, and 2) We need an internal audit trail that can't be tampered with.
[07:31] Priya Desai: SBOM generation is supported. We can produce signed SBOMs per image. For audit trails we can integrate signed append-only logs and export to your SIEM.
[07:40] Lena Ortiz: Also need to confirm retention policy — e.g., logs retained for 7 years for regulatory reasons in some of our jurisdictions.
[07:47] Priya Desai: We'll confirm log retention options and how the exports look; we'll include the retention policy options in the security pack.
[07:55] Alex Kim: Switching gears — POC success criteria? What would you need to see in 6 weeks to feel good?
[08:01] Dr. Maya Gupta: Working POC that demonstrates: ingest of a small pathology dataset, ability to run a classification workflow, throughput numbers within 20% of your estimate, and evidence of the offline update process being workable. Also a security sign-off (Lena).
[08:16] Evan Torres: And we want to ensure the deployment fits our rack/power profile.
[08:20] Priya Desai: We'll size accordingly and give you a proposed mapping.
[08:25] Alex Kim: Sounds good. We'll follow up with the pack and a sizing doc. Any questions from the customer side?
[08:32] Lena Ortiz: One last item — does Redwood offer a remote support mode for troubleshooting if the nodes are offline?
[08:38] Priya Desai: We offer a support package where support engineers can supply runnable artifacts and step-by-step instructions. For fully airgapped systems, remote debugging requires a temporary secure tunnel established by your infra team; otherwise we provide detailed logs and runbooks.
[08:55] Dr. Maya Gupta: OK, that's acceptable.
[09:00] Alex Kim: We'll put all of this into the follow-up. Priya, any final technical notes?
[09:05] Priya Desai: We'll include: hardware compatibility, image signing flow, SBOM and signing, KMS/HSM integration options, log export and retention, and a POC plan with milestones. We'll also recommend a fallback single-node plan if rack constraints force us to limit cluster size.
[09:23] Evan Torres: Anything else re: the model itself? Licensing? Are we allowed to run open models or do we need special licenses for quant variants?
[09:31] Priya Desai: Typically open models are fine; we can provide a list of vetted model artifacts and any associated licenses. Some quantized variants may be redistributed under certain licenses; we'll call that out.
[09:45] Dr. Maya Gupta: Can you sketch the lead times for hardware if we need to procure servers?
[09:50] Alex Kim: We'll include vendor recommendations and lead time estimates — 4-8 weeks for new racks or chassis depending on supply. For POC we usually co-locate on existing hardware.
[10:01] --- (conversation continues with clarifications and small interruptions; meeting has natural cross-talk and short silences) ---
[49:00] Alex Kim: Alright wrapping up — recap: Alex will send security pack and SOC2 summary; Priya will produce HW sizing/POC plan; Evan will share rack/GPU inventory; Lena will provide audit retention needs. We'll propose a workshop on 2026-10-14 for update workflow.
[49:20] Dr. Maya Gupta: That timeline works. Appreciate the clarity.
[49:25] Evan Torres: Thanks everyone.
[49:28] Priya Desai: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs.
[49:31] Alex Kim: Thanks all — talk soon.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-generated, occasional misattributions (e.g., "Redwood Privet"), shorthand (KV cash vs KV cache) and small word errors present.
